title: Van Gogh Painting Sells for a Record $190.4 Million
summary: A painting by Vincent van Gogh has sold at auction for a record $190.4 million. Auction house Sotheby's sold Chestnut Trees in Blossom, known in French as Chataigniers en fleurs, in New York on Wednesday, November 19. The sale shattered Van Gogh's previous auction record of $117.2 million, set in 2022. The oil painting had been estimated to be worth $180 million before the sale. It was not immediately clear who bought the painting. Van Gogh painted it in 1890, in the final two months of his life. Sotheby's considers it one of the most important works of art from that period still in private hands. The painting was sold as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection. The historic sale came after an agreement was reached at the last minute to resolve a dispute about the painting's past. Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family, the prior German owners of the work, had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress, or under pressure, during the rise of the Nazis. A lawyer for the heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's saying the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. Sotheby's said that, in recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution, and the work would be sold under their agreement. Sotheby's website traces how the painting changed hands since 1890. Samuel Fischer, a famous German publisher, acquired it in 1909, and it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934. The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933, before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936. Four other owners then had the painting. The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale.
why_it_matters: Famous paintings are worth huge sums, but their histories can include injustice, so how auction houses handle that past matters for fairness and for remembering history.

background_read: Vincent van Gogh was a Dutch painter whose bold, colorful pictures became famous after his death, and his works now sell for huge sums.
Paintings are often sold at auction, where buyers compete by offering higher and higher prices until only one buyer is left.
Some artworks have a troubled history: during the Nazi era, Jewish families were sometimes forced to sell art under pressure, and their heirs still seek fair treatment today.
Before a big sale, auction houses research who owned a painting over time, which is why this sale followed a last-minute agreement between the two families.
